text: {"user":"I’m planning a birthday gift for my sister and she mentioned she’s been wanting a weekly meal-prep kit. I already picked out a recipe card subscription and I’m also considering adding an insulated food container set so the prepared meals stay fresh for a few days. What details should I make sure to confirm so the gift is actually usable for her?","plus_response":"Since you’re adding a meal-prep kit + containers, confirm a few compatibility details: her dietary preferences (any allergens, vegetarian/low-sodium/etc.), whether she has the storage space (and a microwave/oven for reheating), and how long the recipes typically need to keep. Also double-check whether the subscription already includes portioning/storage guidance—if it does, you can downgrade or cancel the extra container set and spend only on what she truly needs. For the container set, confirm sizes that match typical servings, lid tightness, and whether they’re dishwasher-safe. If she already has suitable containers, it may be better to skip the set and stick to the subscription plus something smaller that matches her routines.","minus_response":"To make sure the gift will be usable, confirm the practical fit for her habits: her dietary preferences and any allergies, whether she’s preparing single portions or family-size meals, and what equipment she has for cooking and reheating. For the recipe card subscription, check that the format matches what she’ll use (printed cards vs. app access) and that the recipes cover the meal length she wants for a few days of leftovers. For the insulated food container set, confirm capacity (how many meals/day she plans to pack), lid quality for keeping things fresh, and heat/cold compatibility. If she’s looking for weekly meal prep, pairing the subscription with quality containers is a nice upgrade because it supports the full routine from cooking to packing and storage."}
